items.title: TSD-TRS-25-006, GRT Ridership Update - Q1 2025
notes:
Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation services, provided an overview of the report, indicating improvements to service for Grand River Transit (GRT) and MobilityPLUS. He also expanded on issues outlined in the report related to service, including a decrease in system ridership. D. Spooner spoke to the plan and associated recommendations for addressing the decrease in ridership, noting the scalability of the GRT Business Plan.

In response to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner provided further clarity as to the purported causes of the decrease in ridership. Furthermore, he elaborated on the 'school specials,' indicating there is not a significant usage of this service and there is a lack of provincial funding. D. Spooner confirmed work is being completed to assist those affected by this change, and that this service is only happening in Cambridge.

Replying to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner spoke to the metrics for on-time performance numbers, and improvements being made to ensure quicker and more efficient stops. He elaborated on efficiency practices and noted staff are continually looking for ways to improve.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner confirmed that the business plan for the Light Rail Train (LRT) to Cambridge is being commenced in August, including the process for public engagement, with a November decision date. Furthermore, D. Spooner clarified that staff have sent letters of support to the province regarding the train line to Guelph/Guelph-Eramosa. Staff are waiting on a plan, and a go bus service is in place in the interim.

In reply to a question from the Committee, Neil Malcolm, Director, Transit Services, indicated the operational efficiency primarily comes from scheduling practices and vehicle capacity.

In response to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner confirmed some bus stops were eliminated, but that stop-specific concerns can be shared with Transit staff.

items.title: TSD-TRS-25-007, GRT Business Plan Approval
notes:
D. Spooner provided an introduction to the GRT Business Plan approval, outlining the positives to the plan, including its scalability. He elaborated on the elements of affordability of transit, describing transit as a cost-effective alternative to car ownership. D. Spooner spoke to barriers to entry for seniors to use GRT service, and recommended the Service Assistant program be utilized to better assist seniors.

In reply to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner clarified those that use Kiwanis program cannot use the taxi trips program, but with the expansion in the Township transit plan, there are opportunities for alignment.

Provided information on the various ways that fares are collected.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner expanded on the cost of adding and redesigning new roads, and confirmed that staff will report back with a comparison for the costs associated with investing in transit versus road enhancements. Furthermore, staff will try to have cost comparisons in future reports.

In response to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner clarified that the business plan provides for the same fare as in Townships to travel anywhere in the network. Furthermore, D. Spooner answered that staff can look at zoned payment structure based on service levels.

Replying to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner answered that there is not a high school program for transit, and staff are seeking a u-pass program for employers and high school students.

Responding to a question from the Committee, D. Spooner explained that the pilot for the equalization program for non-for-profit agencies providing fares is ongoing, and that a report can come back in fall of 2025 to reveal the results of the program.

items.title: Strategic Priority - Resilient and Future Ready Organization
EES-SAM-25-002, 2025 Asset Management Plan
notes:
J. Rose provided an introduction, with Katie Johnson, Director, Strategic Initiatives & Asset Management, providing a presentation on the Asset Management Plan, elaborating on the various components of the plan for asset maintenance and cost, as well as levels of service. She spoke to the funding strategy for the plan, outlining the optimal renewal strategy to minimize the overall cost. Nicole Neil, Director, Corporate Finance, added that there is a focus related to provincial priorities as well as Regional Housing Initiatives, and outlined how the infrastructure renewal policy guides the asset management plan.

In reply to a question from the Committee, J. Rose provided that every budget prepared has decision points based on the guidelines from Council, with some projects being delayed consequently, which results in a backlog. Wayne Steffler, Commissioner, Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, added that understanding the trade off of growth versus maintenance is part of the task.

Responding to a question from the Committee, J. Rose answered that staff are working on incorporating a carbon framework into asset management plan, and all projects are being considered with green infrastructure to keep carbon emissions low. W. Steffler added that there is also an aspect for carbon emission reduction in business cases. Furthermore, he indicated that there are capital budget steering committees in place discussing priorities and affordability. Staff are considering provincial and federal policy changes, and will be following up with a development charge sustainability report to Council.

Replying to a question from the Committee, W. Steffler answered about appropriate timing for capital project requests. Mathieu Goetzke, Acting CAO, elaborated on the strategic plans provided by each department, which will be presented during budget processes, as well as the Integrated Mobility Plan, which would be an appropriate time to discuss bridges. He further clarified that the road system in Cambridge is part of the Integrated Mobility Plan.
